name: Robust Decision-making & Learning Lab (Hanna Kurniawati)
topics: pomdps;planning under uncertainty;meta-rl;integrated planning and learning;robotics
summary: The lab develops scalable solvers for sequential decision making under uncertainty (POMDPs), integrated planning and learning, and reinforcement learning for robots.
question: How can robots operate reliably, resiliently and safely by making principled sequential decisions under uncertainty?

name: Peter Vamplew group (Peter Vamplew)
institution: Federation University Australia (Institute of Innovation, Science and Sustainability)
topics: multi-objective rl;ai safety;distributional rl;value alignment;explainable ai
summary: The group works on multi-objective reinforcement learning and its use for AI safety and explainability, including value-based MORL in stochastic environments and generalisation across environments.
question: How can reinforcement learning handle multiple conflicting objectives to make autonomous systems safer and more explainable?

name: Hao Wang group (Hao Wang)
topics: constrained rl;actor-critic;interpretable rl;energy systems;smart grids
summary: The group applies machine learning, including constrained and interpretable actor-critic reinforcement learning, to smart grids and power and energy systems.
question: How can machine learning and reinforcement learning make energy systems efficient and reliable?

name: Sriram Ganapathi Subramanian group (Sriram Ganapathi Subramanian)
topics: multi-agent rl;mean-field rl;reward machines;game theory;cooperation
summary: The group works on multi-agent reinforcement learning at the intersection with game theory, addressing scale, non-stationarity, communication and safety.
question: How can multi-agent learning systems overcome scale, non-stationarity, communication and sample-inefficiency problems?

name: Khimya Khetarpal (Google DeepMind Montreal)
topics: affordances;self-predictive representations;temporal abstraction;planning;continual adaptation
summary: Works on how RL agents represent world knowledge through affordances and self-predictive representations, plan with temporal abstractions, and adapt over time.
question: How can agents efficiently represent the world's knowledge, plan with it, and adapt to changes over time through interaction?

name: Pablo Samuel Castro (Google DeepMind Montreal)
institution: Google DeepMind; Université de Montréal (adjunct); Mila
topics: deep rl scaling;network plasticity and sparsity;multitask rl;evaluation methodology;atari benchmarks
summary: Studies the training dynamics, scaling and evaluation of deep RL agents, including gradient stability and representation learning for multitask deep RL.
question: What makes deep reinforcement learning networks train stably and scale with more parameters and tasks?

name: Masset Lab (Paul Masset)
topics: distributional rl;dopamine;multiple discount horizons;neural computation
summary: The lab models how heterogeneous neuron types support distributed computations such as dopamine-based distributional and multi-horizon reinforcement learning, and tests these models experimentally.
question: How could dopamine-based distributed reinforcement learning be implemented in brain circuits?

name: David Meger group (David Meger)
topics: off-policy rl;goal-conditioned rl;distributional rl;mobile robotics
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning for robots, including off-policy value learning, goal-conditioned RL and distributional RL theory.
question: How can robots learn reliable control policies from interaction with reinforcement learning?

name: Hsiu-Chin Lin group (Hsiu-Chin Lin)
topics: safe rl;legged locomotion;world models;robot manipulation
summary: The group works on robot learning and control, including safe RL with recovery, value learning and world models for cross-embodiment quadrupedal locomotion.
question: How can robots learn safe and robust control policies for locomotion and manipulation?

name: Learning in Neural Circuits Lab – LiNC (Blake Richards)
topics: continual rl;successor features;eligibility traces;credit assignment;neuroai
summary: The lab studies learning in neural circuits and brain-inspired deep learning, including continual reinforcement learning with fast and slow successor features and eligibility-trace credit assignment.
question: How do neural circuits learn, and what can deep learning and reinforcement learning reveal about learning in the brain?

name: Prakash Panangaden group (Prakash Panangaden)
topics: bisimulation metrics;markov processes;preference-based rl;representation learning
summary: The group studies probabilistic processes and their RL applications, including behavioural pseudometrics, representations in actor-critic methods and preference-based RL.
question: How can behavioural metrics on probabilistic processes inform representation and learning in RL?

name: Siamak Ravanbakhsh group (Siamak Ravanbakhsh)
topics: symmetry;model-based offline rl;exploration;generative modelling;sequential decision making
summary: The group studies probabilistic reasoning, generative modelling and sequential decision making, with RL work on model-based offline RL, sampling-based exploration and symmetry.
question: How can symmetry and generative modelling improve probabilistic reasoning and sequential decision making?

name: Doina Precup group (Doina Precup)
topics: options;planning under uncertainty;plasticity;policy optimization;rl in medicine
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning, temporal abstraction (options), and reasoning and planning under uncertainty, with applications in medicine and control.
question: How can agents use temporal abstraction and planning to learn and act under uncertainty?

name: Oak Lab (Richard S. Sutton; Khurram Javed)
topics: oak architecture;temporal abstraction;streaming rl;step-size adaptation;big world hypothesis
summary: Builds the OaK architecture for agents that learn continually from experience with batch-size-one, replay-free algorithms and plan with learned temporal abstractions.
question: How can agents discover and implement algorithms to achieve goals in big worlds by learning directly from experience?

name: Openmind Research Institute (Joseph Modayil; Richard S. Sutton)
topics: real-time rl;continual learning;robot platforms for rl;temporal-difference methods;open research
summary: A Canadian non-profit institute that funds research fellows and publishes open-source basic research following the Alberta Plan, including real-time RL robot platforms and streaming/differential TD methods.
question: How can minds form from computation interacting with a general continuing data stream and learn in real time from sensorimotor experience?

name: Chandar Research Lab, CRL (Sarath Chandar)
topics: lifelong learning;streaming rl;safe rl;rl for materials discovery;deep learning
summary: The lab develops interactive learning algorithms that learn continuously from experience, including streaming and lifelong RL, constrained RL and RL benchmarks for materials discovery.
question: How can we develop interactive learning algorithms that continuously learn from experiences?

name: Amir-massoud Farahmand group (Amir-massoud Farahmand)
institution: Polytechnique Montréal; Mila; University of Toronto (status-only)
topics: model-based rl;plasticity;policy optimization;rl theory;control
summary: The group studies the computational and statistical mechanisms of efficient RL agents, including decision-aware model learning, policy optimisation and plasticity in continual RL.
question: What computational and statistical mechanisms are required to design efficient RL agents that adaptively improve their long-term performance?

name: Xue Bin (Jason) Peng group (Xue Bin Peng)
primary: RL for character and humanoid motion
topics: motion imitation;physics-based animation;humanoid control;adversarial imitation
summary: The group works at the intersection of computer graphics and machine learning, using reinforcement learning for motion control of simulated characters and humanoid robots.
question: How can reinforcement learning produce natural, versatile motor skills for simulated characters and robots?

name: Adam White group (Adam White)
topics: continual rl;partial observability;empirical methodology;actor-critic;real-world rl
summary: The group models intelligence as an RL agent continually interacting with an unknown environment, with work on continual-learning testbeds, recurrent agents, actor-critic design and RL for industrial control.
question: How can intelligence be modelled as a reinforcement-learning agent that continually interacts with an unknown environment and learns from a scalar reward?

name: Intelligent Robot Learning Lab, IRL Lab (Matthew E. Taylor)
topics: human-in-the-loop rl;reward learning;transfer learning;multi-agent rl;real-world rl
summary: The lab does reinforcement learning research and applies it in simulated and physical settings, with a focus on human-in-the-loop RL, reward learning from human feedback and transfer.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents learn efficiently in real-world settings, including from human feedback?

name: Levi Lelis group (Levi H. S. Lelis)
topics: programmatic policies;program synthesis;tree search;options;combinatorial search
summary: The group develops combinatorial search algorithms for finding programmatic representations, such as computer programs encoding policies and options, for sequential decision-making problems.
question: How can search find programmatic representations, such as programs encoding policies, that solve reinforcement learning problems?

name: Marlos C. Machado group (Marlos C. Machado)
primary: representation learning and options in RL
topics: options;laplacian representations;exploration;continual rl;arcade learning environment
summary: The group studies representation learning, temporally-extended exploration with options, Laplacian/successor-style representations and continual RL.
question: How can agents learn representations and temporally-extended behaviours (options) that support exploration, planning and continual learning?

name: Martha White group (Martha White)
topics: actor-critic;offline hyperparameter selection;real-world rl;replay;value-based methods
summary: The group develops prediction and control algorithms that learn and adapt during deployment, with empirical studies of actor-critic and value-based methods and applications to industrial control such as water treatment.
question: How can prediction and control systems learn and adapt reliably during deployment in the real world?

name: Michael Bowling group (Michael Bowling)
topics: imperfect-information games;exploration;monitored mdps;multi-agent learning;agent computation
summary: The group studies how agents learn through experience, with work on imperfect-information games such as poker, multi-agent learning, exploration and monitored MDPs.
question: How can computers learn to act and play games well through experience?

name: Patrick M. Pilarski group (Patrick M. Pilarski)
topics: continual rl;prosthetics;human-machine interaction;prediction learning;rehabilitation robotics
summary: The group applies continual reinforcement and prediction learning to human-machine partnerships such as intelligent prostheses and rehabilitation devices, as PI in the RLAI and BLINC labs.
question: How can continually learning agents form effective partnerships with people, for example in intelligent prosthetic limbs?

name: Reinforcement Learning and Artificial Intelligence Lab, RLAI (Richard S. Sutton)
primary: continual RL and the Alberta Plan
topics: temporal-difference learning;continual learning;average-reward rl;options and planning;step-size adaptation
summary: Sutton works on the simple general principles of learning from experience (temporal-difference learning, continual learning, average-reward RL, the Alberta Plan and OaK architecture) as a quarter-time professor at the University of Alberta, with most of his current research done at the startup Oak Lab.
question: What simple general principles underlie both natural and artificial intelligence, and how can an agent learn them from its own experience?

name: Rupam Mahmood group (A. Rupam Mahmood)
primary: continual and streaming RL for robots
topics: continual rl;streaming deep rl;real-time robot learning;loss of plasticity;policy gradient
summary: The group develops continual reinforcement and representation learning algorithms and real-time learning systems, including streaming deep RL and RL that runs onboard physical robots.
question: What scalable and general learning mechanisms let agents keep improving continually, including when controlling physical robots in real time?

name: Csaba Szepesvári group (Csaba Szepesvári)
institution: University of Alberta; Amii; Google DeepMind
topics: rl theory;bandits;exploration;robust mdps;learning theory
summary: The group creates and analyses algorithms for efficient sequential decision making, including bandit algorithms, RL theory and connections between RL and control.
question: How can algorithms learn efficiently and effectively in sequential decision making, with provable guarantees?

name: Dale Schuurmans group (Dale Schuurmans)
institution: University of Alberta; Amii; Google DeepMind
primary: RL foundations and RL for reasoning
topics: rl for llm reasoning;representation learning;policy optimization;big world hypothesis
summary: The group works on foundations of RL and representation learning, including spectral representations for RL and reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning.
question: Which representations and optimisation principles make reinforcement learning efficient, including for training models to reason?

name: Michiel van de Panne group (Michiel van de Panne)
topics: character animation;legged locomotion;deep rl;motion planning
summary: The group uses deep reinforcement learning for agile human motion, legged locomotion, physics-based character animation and robot control.
question: How can simulated characters and robots learn agile, skilful motion?

name: Jeff Clune group (Jeff Clune)
institution: University of British Columbia; Vector Institute
topics: open-endedness;exploration;self-play;ai-generating algorithms;self-improving agents
summary: The group works on open-ended algorithms, AI-generating algorithms and self-improving agents, including foundation-model self-play and exploration methods descended from Go-Explore.
question: How can we create open-ended algorithms that keep innovating and learning forever?

name: Data-Driven Decision Making Lab, D3M (Scott Sanner)
topics: model-based planning;offline rl;multi-agent rl;traffic control
summary: The lab works on sequential decision making alongside recommendation, including offline model-based planning, multi-agent RL and RL for traffic control.
question: How can rich sources of data be turned into optimal and actionable sequential decisions?

name: Learning, Embodied Autonomy, and Forecasting Lab, LEAF (Nicholas Rhinehart)
topics: reward learning;preference-based rl;forecasting;model-based control
summary: The lab works on general-purpose model-based control by combining learned world models (forecasting) with learned objectives (reward learning), including preference-based RL.
question: How can autonomous systems combine accurate world models with learned objectives to perform a wide range of tasks?

name: Robot Vision & Learning Lab, RVL (Florian Shkurti)
topics: offline-to-online rl;imitation learning;robot manipulation;robot policies
summary: The lab works on robot learning, including offline-to-online actor-critic transfer, imitation learning and evaluation of robot policies.
question: How can robots learn robust control policies from data and interaction?

name: Sheila McIlraith group (Sheila A. McIlraith)
primary: reward machines and formal methods in RL
topics: reward machines;formal languages;symbolic planning;language grounding
summary: The group combines knowledge representation, formal languages and planning with reinforcement learning, including reward machines and grounding language in agent behaviour.
question: How can formal languages and symbolic knowledge, such as reward machines, make reinforcement learning agents more sample-efficient and aligned?

name: Toronto Intelligent Systems Lab, TISL (Igor Gilitschenski)
topics: goal-conditioned rl;model-based rl;reward hacking;embodied ai
summary: The lab works on embodied AI and robot learning, including goal-conditioned and value-aware model-based RL and reward-hacking detection.
question: How can embodied agents learn efficiently in simulation and the real world, inspired by human learning?

name: Mark Crowley group (Mark Crowley)
topics: machine ethics;social rl;bandits;multi-agent decision making
summary: The group studies decision making for single and multiple agents, including how ethical or moral requirements change the definition of reinforcement learning.
question: How do the structure and challenges of ethical or moral requirements affect how we define learning and decision making?

name: Pascal Poupart group (Pascal Poupart)
topics: multi-agent rl;inverse constrained rl;bayesian rl;offline model-based planning
summary: The group works on sequential decision making under uncertainty, including multi-agent RL, inverse constrained RL and Bayesian model-based planning.
question: How can agents make good sequential decisions under uncertainty, alone and with other agents?

name: Audrey Durand group (Audrey Durand)
topics: bandits;multi-objective rl;rl fine-tuning;adaptive experiments
summary: The group works on bandits and reinforcement learning, including multi-objective RL, RL fine-tuning of language models and adaptive experimentation.
question: How can bandit and RL algorithms make sample-efficient sequential decisions in real applications?

name: Aaron Courville group (Aaron Courville)
primary: deep RL and RL for LLMs
topics: rl for llms;network scaling in rl;plasticity;deep learning
summary: The group works on deep learning with a substantial deep-RL line, including RL fine-tuning of language models and architecture and scaling studies for deep RL agents.
question: How can deep networks be trained with reinforcement learning to scale and to solve hard problems?

name: Pierre-Luc Bacon group (Pierre-Luc Bacon)
topics: offline rl;model-based rl;optimal control;long horizons;rl for energy systems
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning and optimal control, particularly the curse of the horizon and representation learning, with applications to HVAC/energy, materials and drug discovery.
question: How can representation learning and ideas from optimal control help RL overcome the curse of the horizon?

name: Robotics and Embodied AI Lab, REAL (Glen Berseth; Liam Paull)
topics: robot learning;safe exploration;generalization;rl benchmarks;embodied agents
summary: The lab works on sequential decision making for robots and other embodied agents, including RL for generalist robots, safe exploration and benchmarks for RL agents.
question: How can we build generalist robots and embodied agents that learn to make sequential decisions in the real world?

name: Qwen Team RL (Alibaba)
topics: sequence-level policy optimization;mixture-of-experts rl stability;soft clipping;reasoning models;rl infrastructure
summary: Develops RL algorithms for training Qwen language models, including Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) and Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization (SAPO).
question: How can RL training of large (including mixture-of-experts) language models be made stable and efficient?

name: Gang Wang group (Gang Wang)
institution: Beijing Institute of Technology (School of Automation)
topics: world models;multi-task rl;offline rl;whole-body control;data-driven control
summary: The group applies control, optimisation and reinforcement learning to multi-agent and cyber-physical systems, including transformer world models (STORM) and modular world models for multi-task RL.
question: How can control, optimization and reinforcement learning be applied to multi-agent networks and cyber-physical systems?

name: ByteDance Seed LLM RL (Mingxuan Wang)
topics: policy optimization;value-based rl for reasoning;long chain-of-thought;open rl systems;math and code reasoning
summary: Develops open large-scale RL algorithms and systems for reasoning language models, including DAPO and value-augmented PPO (VAPO).
question: How can reinforcement learning for long chain-of-thought reasoning be made stable, efficient and reproducible at scale?

name: ByteDance Seed Robotics (Hang Li)
topics: vision-language-action models;real-world rl;dexterous long-horizon manipulation;multi-task critics;demonstration filtering
summary: Develops GR-series robot policies and GR-RL, which augments a generalist vision-language-action model with reinforcement learning for precise long-horizon manipulation.
question: How can generalist robot policies be turned into reliable specialists for dexterous long-horizon tasks?

name: Biao Luo group (Biao Luo)
topics: adaptive dynamic programming;multi-agent rl;multi-objective rl;intelligent control;rl for design
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning and adaptive dynamic programming for intelligent control, including multi-agent and preference-based multi-objective RL and RL-guided molecular design.
question: How can reinforcement learning and adaptive dynamic programming deliver optimal decisions and control in complex systems?

name: Computational and Integrative Cognition Lab (Yunzhe Liu)
institution: Chinese Institute for Brain Research, Beijing (CIBR); Beijing Normal University
primary: replay and planning in the brain
topics: neural replay;model-based learning;planning;cognitive maps;computational psychiatry
summary: The lab studies the neural and computational basis of flexible behaviour in humans, focusing on hippocampal replay, model-based learning and planning, and cognitive maps.
question: How can we learn so much from so little and make flexible decisions in novel contexts?

name: Shuang Qiu group (Shuang Qiu)
institution: City University of Hong Kong (Department of Data Science)
topics: offline rl;cross-domain rl;robust rl;model-based rl;llm agents
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning theory and algorithms, including robust cross-domain and model-based offline RL, and RL-based credit assignment for language-model agents.
question: How can agents learn reliable policies from offline data collected under shifted dynamics?

name: DeepSeek (Liang Wenfeng)
topics: grpo;rl-incentivized reasoning;self-verifiable math reasoning;mixture-of-experts llms;reasoning models
summary: Trains open language models whose reasoning is developed through reinforcement learning with the GRPO algorithm (DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeekMath-V2).
question: Can the reasoning abilities of large language models be incentivized through pure reinforcement learning?

name: Xiangfeng Wang group (Xiangfeng Wang)
institution: East China Normal University (School of Computer Science and Technology)
topics: multi-agent rl;offline marl;reward machines;multi-agent pathfinding;llm agents
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning and multi-agent RL, including conservative offline MARL, reward-machine transfer and learned multi-agent pathfinding, and LLM-based agents.
question: How can teams of learning agents coordinate and transfer knowledge across tasks?

name: STAIR Lab (Hao Su)
institution: Fudan University (Institute of General Physical Intelligence)
topics: massively parallel rl;robot simulation;world models;manipulation;embodied ai
summary: The lab works on embodied AI and robot learning, including GPU-parallel simulation (ManiSkill), massively parallel on-policy RL and world models for control.
question: How can simulation, large-scale reinforcement learning and world models give robots a real understanding of the physical world?

name: Ling Pan group (Ling Pan)
institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Department of Electronic and Computer Engineering)
topics: deep rl;plasticity;gflownets;multi-agent rl;rl for llms
summary: The group works on the theory, algorithms and applications of deep reinforcement learning, GFlowNets and multi-agent systems, including network plasticity in deep RL and RL for language-model post-training.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning and multi-agent decision-making algorithms be made robust, efficient and practical?

name: Deep Reinforcement Learning Group, CASIA (Dongbin Zhao)
institution: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA); UCAS
topics: deep rl;multi-agent rl;autonomous driving;embodied ai;llm agents
summary: The group studies deep and multi-agent RL and applies it to intelligent driving, embodied intelligence, game AI and agent training.
question: How can deep and multi-agent reinforcement learning be advanced and applied to driving, embodied and game intelligence?

name: Moonshot AI Kimi Team (Yang Zhilin)
topics: long-context rl;agentic rl;reasoning models;policy optimization;open-weight models
summary: Trains the Kimi language models with large-scale reinforcement learning for long-context reasoning and agentic tasks.
question: How can reinforcement learning be scaled to train language models for long-horizon reasoning and agentic use?

name: LAMDA reinforcement learning group (Yang Yu)
topics: model-based rl;offline rl;world models;multi-agent coordination;vla policy optimization
summary: The group develops model-based, offline and multi-agent RL methods, including world-model-based policy optimization for vision-language-action agents.
question: How can learned environment models make reinforcement learning sample-efficient enough for real-world decision-making?

name: Zongzhang Zhang group (Zongzhang Zhang)
institution: Nanjing University (LAMDA; School of Artificial Intelligence)
topics: deep rl;reward models;multi-agent coordination;safe autonomous driving;online rl
summary: The group studies deep and multi-agent RL, reward models for RL, and online RL for safety-critical settings such as autonomous driving.
question: How can reward design, coordination and online adaptation make deep reinforcement learning reliable in multi-agent and safety-critical settings?

name: Reasoning and Learning Research Group (Yang Gao)
institution: Nanjing University (School of Intelligence Science and Technology)
topics: multi-agent rl;decentralized cooperation;causal rl;model-based rl;game theory
summary: The group studies multi-agent and single-agent reinforcement learning, including communication-constrained and decentralized cooperative MARL and causal structure learning for model-based RL.
question: How can multiple learning agents cooperate efficiently under limited communication and partial information?

name: Chunlin Chen group (Chunlin Chen)
institution: Nanjing University (School of Management and Engineering)
topics: in-context rl;multi-agent q-learning;sim-to-real;imitation learning;quantum control
summary: The group develops reinforcement learning methods, including in-context Q-learning, interpretable multi-agent Q-learning and sim-to-real transfer, with applications in robotics and quantum control.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents adapt quickly to new tasks and transfer from simulation to real systems?

name: Ruosong Wang group (Ruosong Wang)
institution: Peking University (Center on Frontiers of Computing Studies)
topics: rl theory;sample complexity;function approximation;reward-free exploration;lower bounds
summary: The group studies the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning, designing provably efficient algorithms and proving sample-complexity lower bounds under function approximation.
question: What are the fundamental statistical and computational limits of reinforcement learning, and which algorithms reach them?

name: PKU Alignment and Interaction Research Lab (PAIR Lab) (Yaodong Yang)
topics: safe rl;multi-agent rl;game theory;rlhf alignment;robotic rl
summary: The lab works on constrained (safe) RL, multi-agent RL and game theory, and RL-based alignment and robot learning; it maintains open-source safe-RL tools such as Safety-Gymnasium, OmniSafe and Safe-RLHF.
question: How can constrained reinforcement learning and multi-agent game-theoretic modelling make learning agents reliably do what humans intend?

name: Zongqing Lu group (Zongqing Lu)
institution: Peking University (School of Computer Science); BeingBeyond
primary: RL for embodied agents and humanoids
topics: reinforcement learning;multi-agent rl;humanoid control;world models;vision-language-action models
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning, multimodal models and general agents so that robots and agents can acquire skills, cooperate and communicate in open worlds.
question: How can robots and agents autonomously acquire skills to accomplish tasks, cooperate and communicate in the open world?

name: Learning and Optimization Group (Zhihua Zhang)
topics: distributional rl;td learning;policy gradient theory;statistical inference;bandits
summary: The group applies statistical inference, optimisation and stochastic analysis to machine learning, including finite-sample analysis of distributional TD learning and convergence of policy gradient methods.
question: What statistical and optimisation principles explain how learning algorithms, including reinforcement learning, work?

name: Yunbo Wang group (Yunbo Wang)
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Artificial Intelligence Institute, School of Computer Science)
topics: world models;model-based rl;offline rl;humanoid locomotion;embodied ai
summary: The group studies world models and model-based reinforcement learning for embodied agents, including video-enhanced offline RL, open-world imagination-based RL and humanoid locomotion.
question: How can embodied agents use learned world models and imagination to make decisions that generalise across open-world scenarios?

name: Shuai Li group (Shuai Li)
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (John Hopcroft Center for Computer Science)
topics: bandits;rl theory;offline-to-online rl;matching markets;extensive-form games
summary: The group designs reinforcement learning and multi-armed bandit algorithms with regret analysis, including offline-to-online RL, adversarial MDPs and learning in matching markets and games.
question: How can reinforcement learning and bandit algorithms be designed with provable regret guarantees?

name: APEX Lab RL group (Weinan Zhang)
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (School of Computer Science)
topics: reinforcement learning;multi-agent rl;diffusion policies;llm agents;humanoid control
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning, agentic AI and embodied AI, including on-policy RL with generative policies and humanoid whole-body control.
question: How can reinforcement learning make AI agents and embodied systems learn effective decisions from interaction?

name: Advanced Networking and System Research Lab (John C. S. Lui)
institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Department of Computer Science and Engineering)
topics: multi-armed bandits;dueling bandits;rl theory;quantum algorithms for mdps;online learning
summary: Among networking and systems topics, the lab works on online learning algorithms, including multi-armed and dueling bandits, model-based RL and quantum algorithms for MDPs.
question: How can online learning algorithms such as bandits and reinforcement learning be made efficient for networked systems?

name: Baoxiang Wang group (Baoxiang Wang)
institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (School of Data Science)
topics: reinforcement learning;learning in games;multi-agent learning;llm-rl;information design
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning and game theory, including learning in games, multi-agent incentives and RL for language models.
question: How do multiple learning agents learn, reason and coordinate in games and under information design?

name: Embodied Decision Making Lab (Edem) (Guiliang Liu)
institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (School of Data Science)
primary: inverse constrained RL and embodied RL
topics: inverse constrained rl;safe rl;humanoid locomotion;rl from human feedback;robot manipulation
summary: The lab studies reinforcement learning and embodied decision making, including inverse constrained RL that infers safety constraints from demonstrations, and RL for humanoid whole-body control.
question: How can embodied agents infer the constraints behind expert behaviour and act safely in the physical world?

name: Junxian He group (Junxian He)
institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (CSE)
topics: rlvr;llm reasoning;reward models;agents;code generation
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning for reasoning in large language models, including RL from verifiable rewards, reward models and agent training.
question: When and why does reinforcement learning improve the reasoning of language models?

name: Jun Zhang group (Jun Zhang)
institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (ECE)
primary: safe offline RL and world models
topics: safe offline rl;multi-agent rl;world models;rl for llms;edge ai
summary: The group works on safe offline reinforcement learning, multi-agent RL communication and world models, alongside edge AI systems.
question: How can agents learn safe and scalable policies from offline data and learned world models?

name: Deep Reinforcement Learning Lab, Tianjin University (Jianye Hao)
institution: Tianjin University (College of Intelligence and Computing)
topics: deep rl;multi-agent systems;off-policy rl;multi-task rl;decision-making applications
summary: The lab develops deep RL and multi-agent methods, including scalable off-policy and multi-task RL, for large-scale decision problems such as chip design, driving and games.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems solve large-scale, dynamic decision-making problems?

name: Junliang Xing group (Junliang Xing)
institution: Tsinghua University (Department of Computer Science and Technology)
topics: game ai;imperfect-information games;multi-task rl;in-context rl;opponent modeling
summary: The group builds reinforcement-learning agents for adversarial and imperfect-information games (e.g. AlphaHoldem) and studies multi-task, offline and in-context RL and opponent modelling.
question: How can learning agents make strong decisions in adversarial games and other multi-agent settings?

name: Decision Intelligence Lab (Longbo Huang)
topics: reinforcement learning theory;deep rl;multi-agent rl;online learning;network optimization
summary: The lab studies theory and algorithms for decision-making, including deep RL, RL theory, multi-agent flow policies and learning-augmented network optimization.
question: How can efficient, robust and safe AI theory and algorithms be developed for decision making and optimization in networked systems?

name: Intelligent Systems and Robotics Lab (ISR Lab) (Jianyu Chen)
topics: reinforcement learning;humanoid robots;robot control;vision-language-action models;autonomous driving
