summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming for real-time control, including control of wearable robotic devices.
question: How can reinforcement learning control physical devices that interact with people in real time?

name: Boston Dynamics Atlas learning team (Scott Kuindersma; Michael Lutter)
topics: humanoid whole-body control;sim-to-real rl;athletic skills;dexterous manipulation;large behavior models
summary: Trains Atlas humanoid behaviours with RL in simulation and from demonstrations, including zero-shot transfer of athletic skills.
question: How can a humanoid robot acquire general, dynamic whole-body behaviours through reinforcement learning and transfer them to hardware?

name: Dependable Computing Laboratory (Wenchao Li)
topics: safe rl;offline safe rl;temporal logic;multi-agent rl;control barrier functions
summary: The lab works on safe and specification-guided reinforcement learning, including offline safe RL, temporal-logic generalisation and multi-agent RL with control barrier functions.
question: How can learning-enabled systems satisfy formal safety and task specifications?

name: Xuezhou Zhang group (Xuezhou Zhang)
topics: rl theory;rlhf;reward poisoning;exploration;llm reasoning
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning theory, RLHF exploration and adversarial reward poisoning, and RL methods for language-model reasoning.
question: How can reinforcement learning remain efficient and secure when rewards are learned or manipulated?

name: Aldo Pacchiano group (Aldo Pacchiano)
institution: Boston University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
topics: exploration;policy evaluation;reward design;bandits;in-context learning
summary: The group studies exploration, model selection, multi-policy evaluation and reward design in reinforcement learning and bandits.
question: How can agents explore and evaluate policies efficiently when objectives and models are uncertain?

name: Intelligent Robot Lab (George Konidaris)
topics: hierarchical rl;skill discovery;state abstraction;robot planning;rl theory
summary: Studies how agents learn skill and state abstraction hierarchies that support fast, goal-oriented planning, with applications to general-purpose robots.
question: How can an agent learn abstraction hierarchies that enable fast, goal-oriented planning?

name: Michael Littman group
topics: continual model-based rl;reward specification;end-user rl programming;markov decision processes;human-robot interaction
summary: Works on reinforcement learning and its interaction with people, including continual model-based RL and interfaces that let non-experts specify RL tasks for robots.
question: How can people specify and benefit from reinforcement learning agents?

name: Serena Booth group (Serena Booth)
topics: reward design;objective specification;human-ai interaction;human-robot interaction
summary: The group studies how people specify, inspect and revise objectives for RL agents and robots, including reward alignment metrics.
question: How can people specify, inspect and revise the behaviour of AI and robot learners?

name: Laboratory of Neural Computation and Cognition (Michael J. Frank)
institution: Brown University (Carney Institute for Brain Science)
topics: basal ganglia;dopamine;working memory;cognitive control;hierarchical bayesian modelling
summary: The lab builds neural-circuit and algorithmic models of basal ganglia–cortex interactions underlying reinforcement learning, decision making and cognitive control, and tests them with experiments.
question: What neural mechanisms underlie reinforcement learning, decision making and cognitive control?

name: Eric Mazumdar group (Eric Mazumdar)
topics: multi-agent rl;game theory;robust rl;risk-averse learning;behavioral economics
summary: The group studies learning in strategic multi-agent environments, including robust and risk-averse multi-agent reinforcement learning.
question: How should learning algorithms behave when they interact with other strategic learners and people?

name: Adam Wierman group
primary: robust and safe RL for systems
topics: robust constrained mdps;sim-to-real safety;multi-agent rl;learning-augmented control;networked systems
summary: Develops RL and learning-augmented control with provable guarantees (robust constrained MDPs, safe sim-to-real, multi-agent RL) for networked systems.
question: How can learning-based control be made provably robust for the networked systems that govern society?

name: AI & Reinforcement Learning Lab (AIRe) (Aviral Kumar)
primary: scaling RL; offline RL; RL for LLMs
topics: offline rl;value-based rl;rl for llm reasoning;robot rl;test-time compute
summary: Builds reinforcement learning and sequential decision-making algorithms, from value-based and offline RL to RL training of language models and real robots.
question: How can reinforcement learning be scaled to train AI systems that act autonomously in open-world settings?

name: Aarti Singh group (Aarti Singh)
topics: interactive learning;rlvr;multi-objective rl;bandits;text feedback
summary: The group studies interactive and sequential learning, including reinforcement learning from text feedback, RLVR dynamics and multi-objective RL.
question: How can learners use richer, adaptive feedback to learn decisions efficiently?

name: Andrea Zanette group
topics: rl with verifiable rewards;llm reasoning;rl theory;efficient reasoning
summary: Studies reinforcement learning for training and aligning foundation models, including variance reduction and efficiency in RL post-training of reasoning models.
question: How can reinforcement learning make foundation-model reasoning more efficient and better aligned?

name: Electronic Marketplaces Laboratory (Tuomas Sandholm)
topics: imperfect-information games;equilibrium finding;multi-agent learning;game-playing agents;mechanism design
summary: Develops algorithms for solving large imperfect-information games and multi-agent decision problems, combining game theory with learning and search.
question: How can agents compute strong strategies in large games with hidden information?

name: Fei Fang group
topics: multi-agent rl;game theory;rl from human feedback;rl for llms;ai for social good
summary: Combines machine learning and multi-agent systems, including multi-agent RL from human feedback and RL training of language models.
question: How can reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning be combined with large language models for multi-agent decision-making?

name: Jeff Schneider group (Auton Lab)
topics: offline rl;model-based rl;plasma control;llm agents;robot learning
summary: Works on reinforcement learning and decision making, including offline and model-based RL for tokamak plasma control, robotics and LLM agents.
question: How can agents learn reliable control policies from limited or offline data in high-stakes physical systems?

name: LeCAR Lab (Guanya Shi)
topics: humanoid control;sim-to-real rl;rl and mpc;whole-body control;dexterous manipulation
summary: Develops learning and control methods, including reinforcement learning combined with model-based control, for agile humanoids and other generalist robots.
question: How can learning and control be combined to make generalist robots reliable, adaptive and agile?

name: Safe AI Lab (Ding Zhao)
topics: safe rl;humanoid robots;autonomous driving;human-robot collaboration;multi-agent rl
summary: Develops learning methods for trustworthy physical AI agents, including safe and multi-agent reinforcement learning for humanoids, robots and autonomous vehicles.
question: How can generalist AI agents be made trustworthy for safety-critical physical applications?

name: Max Simchowitz group (Max Simchowitz)
topics: imitation learning;behavior cloning;diffusion policies;policy optimization;control theory
summary: The group studies the theory and practice of imitation learning and RL fine-tuning of generative control policies for robotics.
question: When and why do imitation learning and RL fine-tuning of generative policies succeed in control?

name: Robots Perceiving and Doing Lab (David Held)
topics: robot manipulation;deformable objects;world models;policy adaptation;assistive robotics
summary: The lab develops perception and learning methods, including reinforcement learning and policy adaptation, for robot manipulation of deformable and articulated objects.
question: How can robots perceive and act in cluttered everyday environments?

name: Deepak Pathak group
primary: RL for robot locomotion and manipulation
topics: legged locomotion;sim-to-real rl;dexterous manipulation;humanoids;curiosity-driven exploration
summary: Develops learning methods, including reinforcement learning and policy-gradient fine-tuning, for generalist locomotion and dexterous manipulation on real robots.
question: How can robots learn general skills from experience that adapt across bodies, tasks and environments?

name: Causal Artificial Intelligence Lab (Elias Bareinboim)
topics: causal rl;confounding;causal imitation learning;offline rl;credit assignment
summary: The lab develops causal inference methods and causal reinforcement learning, including confounding-robust offline RL and causal imitation learning.
question: How can agents learn and act well when data are confounded and the causal structure is only partly known?

name: Shipra Agrawal group
topics: multi-armed bandits;thompson sampling;rl theory;online learning;operations research
summary: Develops algorithms and theory for multi-armed bandits, online learning and reinforcement learning, with applications in operations research.
question: How should agents learn to make sequential decisions under uncertainty with provable guarantees?

name: Daniel Russo group (Daniel Russo)
topics: thompson sampling;exploration;policy gradient;bandits;sequential decisions
summary: The group studies exploration, Thompson sampling and policy optimisation in sequential decision making.
question: How should an agent explore to learn good decisions efficiently?

name: People and Robots Teaching and Learning (PoRTaL) (Sanjiban Choudhury)
primary: imitation and reinforcement learning for robots
topics: imitation learning;inverse rl;reward learning;llm agents;human-robot interaction
summary: Works on imitation learning, reward learning and reinforcement learning so that robots and agents can learn skills from people.
question: How can robots learn everyday tasks from people in ways that are practical for everyday users?

name: Sarah Dean group
topics: data-driven control;policy gradient;feedback dynamics;recommender systems;system identification
summary: Studies the fundamentals of data-driven control and sequential decision-making, including policy gradient methods and policies for systems with feedback and participation dynamics.
question: How do optimization, machine learning and dynamics interact in data-driven methods for control and decision-making?

name: Wen Sun group (Wen Sun)
topics: rl theory;imitation learning;offline rl;rlhf;llm post-training
summary: The group develops provably efficient reinforcement learning, imitation learning and RL-from-human-feedback algorithms and applies them to post-training of large language models.
question: How can reinforcement and imitation learning be made both provably sample-efficient and practical at scale?

name: Nathan Kallus group (Nathan Kallus)
topics: off-policy evaluation;causal inference;risk-sensitive rl;distributional rl;recommender systems
summary: The group works on causal inference and off-policy reinforcement learning, including risk-sensitive and distributional RL and RL for recommender systems.
question: How can we learn and evaluate decision policies reliably from observational data?

name: General Robotics Lab (Boyuan Chen)
topics: robot learning;preference-based rl;self-imitation learning;legged locomotion;human feedback
summary: Builds robot learning methods including preference-driven RL with language-model feedback, self-imitation RL and RL-trained humanoid locomotion.
question: How can machines learn, act and collaborate by discovering how the world works?

name: Pan Xu Lab (Pan Xu)
topics: robust rl;off-dynamics rl;offline rl;thompson sampling;rl theory
summary: The lab works on statistical and algorithmic foundations of reinforcement learning, with recent focus on distributionally robust MDPs and off-dynamics offline RL.
question: How can agents learn decision policies that transfer reliably across shifts in environment dynamics?

name: Ronald Parr group (Ronald Parr)
topics: linear function approximation;off-policy rl;policy evaluation;planning
summary: The group studies value function approximation and off-policy reinforcement learning, including linear methods and policy sampling.
question: How can value-function approximation be made stable and accurate for off-policy reinforcement learning?

name: CORE Robotics Lab (Matthew Gombolay)
primary: learning from demonstration and multi-robot RL
topics: learning from demonstration;reward learning;multi-robot coordination;interpretable rl;human-robot teaming
summary: The lab develops learning-from-demonstration, reward learning and RL-based scheduling methods for human-robot teams and multi-robot coordination.
question: How can robots learn from heterogeneous human demonstrations and coordinate with people?

name: Guanghui Lan group
topics: policy mirror descent;value mirror descent;exploration;average-reward mdps;stochastic optimization
summary: Designs stochastic optimization algorithms for reinforcement learning, such as policy and value mirror descent and auto-exploration methods for online RL.
question: How can efficient algorithms be designed for the optimization problems arising in reinforcement learning?

name: Ha Lab (Sehoon Ha)
primary: RL for legged and humanoid robots
topics: legged locomotion;sim-to-real;character animation;world models;mobile manipulation
summary: Applies reinforcement learning and world models to legged locomotion, humanoid robots and character animation.
question: How can robots learn agile and stable motor skills that transfer from simulation to the real world?

name: People, AI, and Robotics (PAIR) Lab (Animesh Garg)
topics: robot learning;off-policy rl;dexterous manipulation;representation learning;self-driving labs
summary: Studies representations and algorithms for reinforcement learning and control that let robots acquire and transfer skills.
question: What structured inductive biases let robots acquire generalizable skills for interaction?

name: Siva Theja Maguluri group
topics: stochastic approximation;td learning;q-learning;finite-sample analysis;queueing
summary: Studies finite-sample convergence of the stochastic approximation algorithms that underlie reinforcement learning, such as TD learning and Q-learning.
question: What finite-sample guarantees hold for reinforcement learning algorithms viewed as stochastic approximation?

name: Bo Dai group
institution: Georgia Institute of Technology; Google DeepMind
topics: spectral representations;actor-critic;exploration;agent ai;generative models
summary: Develops reinforcement learning and planning methods built on learned representations and generative models of the world.
question: How can agents gain decision-making and planning ability by modeling the world?

name: Google DeepMind Robotics (Carolina Parada)
topics: vision-language-action models;embodied reasoning;dexterous manipulation;reinforcement learning fine-tuning;motion transfer
summary: Builds the Gemini Robotics vision-language-action and embodied-reasoning models and uses reinforcement learning among other training methods to improve robot dexterity.
question: How can a single generalist model let robots reason about and act in the physical world across many embodiments?

name: Kimberly Stachenfeld (Google DeepMind NYC)
primary: RL and predictive maps in brains
topics: successor representation;hippocampus;dopamine and reinforcement;cognitive models of learning;automated science
summary: Studies how brains build predictive models of the world, linking RL concepts such as the successor representation and dopamine-mediated reinforcement to behaviour and to machine learning models.
question: How do brains build models of the world that support memory and prediction, and how can these functions be implemented in learning systems?

name: Data to Actionable Knowledge Lab (Finale Doshi-Velez)
topics: off-policy evaluation;interpretable rl;healthcare;reward shaping;bandits
summary: The lab develops interpretable and off-policy reinforcement learning methods for healthcare decision support.
question: How can sequential decision models be made interpretable and safe enough to support clinical decisions?

name: Na Li group
primary: control and RL for dynamical systems
topics: model-based rl;multi-agent rl;representation learning;control theory;diffusion policies
summary: Studies the interplay of control and learning, including model-based and model-free reinforcement learning and scalable multi-agent learning for physical systems.
question: How can control theory and reinforcement learning be combined for scalable, reliable decision making in dynamical systems?

name: Uchida Lab (Naoshige Uchida; Mitsuko Watabe-Uchida)
topics: dopamine;distributional rl;temporal difference learning;striatum;value learning
summary: The lab records and manipulates dopamine and striatal circuits in rodents to test reinforcement-learning accounts of reward learning, including distributional and temporal-difference learning.
question: What are the neural mechanisms for learning based on rewards and punishments?

name: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Lab (Samuel Gershman)
institution: Harvard University (Psychology; Center for Brain Science)
topics: dopamine;bayesian rl;structure learning;resource-rational decisions;continual rl
summary: The lab combines behavioural, neural and computational methods to study how the brain learns structured models and uses them for reward-guided behaviour under computational limits, including dopamine-based learning and, with Kempner Fellow Wilka Carvalho, continual RL in humans and machines.
question: How does the brain acquire richly structured knowledge from little data and use it to guide adaptive behaviour under stringent computational limits?

name: Teamcore (Milind Tambe)
topics: restless bandits;multi-objective rl;combinatorial-action rl;public health;resource allocation
summary: Teamcore applies multi-agent systems and reinforcement learning, including restless bandits and combinatorial-action RL, to resource allocation in public health and conservation.
question: How can AI and reinforcement learning allocate scarce resources to improve outcomes for underserved communities?

name: Kianté Brantley group
primary: RL and imitation for foundation models
topics: rl for llms;imitation learning;rlhf;off-policy rl;interactive learning
summary: Studies reinforcement learning and imitation learning methods that improve the decision-making of foundation models from interactive feedback.
question: How can learning from interactive feedback correct misalignment in systems built on foundation models?

name: Sham Kakade group
topics: rl theory;policy optimization;llm training;interactive agents;scaling laws
summary: Works on mathematical foundations of learning systems, including policy optimization and reinforcement learning, and on training pipelines for foundation models and interactive agents.
question: What principles govern large-scale learning systems and agents that learn from interaction?

name: Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab (Susan Murphy)
topics: just-in-time adaptive interventions;online rl;micro-randomized trials;digital health;statistical inference
summary: Develops reinforcement learning and statistical methods for personalizing sequential treatments, including just-in-time adaptive interventions delivered by mobile devices.
question: How can online reinforcement learning safely personalize health interventions delivered in daily life?

name: SMART Lab (Byung-Cheol Min)
topics: preference-based rl;reward learning;multi-robot systems;imitation learning;human-robot interaction
summary: The lab develops robot learning for multi-robot and human-robot teams, including preference-based reinforcement learning and reward learning.
question: How can multiple robots learn to collaborate with each other and with humans?

name: Raman Arora group (Raman Arora)
topics: markov games;policy regret;machine unlearning;partial observability;rl theory
summary: The group develops learning theory for reinforcement learning and Markov games, including policy regret and unlearning in RL.
question: What guarantees can learning agents achieve against adaptive opponents in sequential games?

name: Laixi Shi group (Laixi Shi)
institution: Johns Hopkins University (Electrical and Computer Engineering)
topics: robust rl;multi-agent rl;sim-to-real;rlvr;sample complexity
summary: The group develops robust and multi-agent reinforcement learning with sample-efficiency guarantees and studies safe sim-to-real transfer.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made robust, safe and sample-efficient in multi-agent and real-world settings?

name: Keen Technologies (John Carmack)
topics: physical atari;real-time rl;continual learning;online adaptation;robot platforms
summary: Researches RL agents that learn online from streams of experience, including the Physical Atari platform for real-time RL on robots.
question: How can agents learn efficiently online from real-time streams of experience rather than static datasets?

name: Shibhansh Dohare (Keen Technologies)
city: Dallas (company HQ; personal location not stated)
topics: loss of plasticity;continual backpropagation;weight reinitialization;continual learning;policy collapse
summary: Studies loss of plasticity in deep continual learning and RL and methods such as continual backpropagation and selective weight reinitialization to maintain it.
question: How can neural networks keep learning new things indefinitely without losing plasticity?

name: Alexander Rakhlin group (Alexander Rakhlin)
topics: rl theory;online learning;decision-estimation coefficient;outcome-based rl;process supervision
summary: The group develops statistical and computational theory for interactive decision making, including reinforcement learning, bandits and outcome-based RL for language models.
question: What are the fundamental statistical limits of learning to make decisions interactively?

name: Cathy Wu group
topics: traffic control;multi-agent rl;zero-shot generalization;sociotechnical systems;optimization
summary: Develops data-driven decision methods, including reinforcement learning, for modeling, control and optimization of transportation and other sociotechnical systems.
question: How can data-driven methods enable faster, evidence-based decisions for sociotechnical systems such as transportation?

name: Gabriele Farina group (Gabriele Farina)
topics: imperfect-information games;policy gradient;equilibrium computation;multi-agent learning;reward models
summary: The group studies multi-agent learning and equilibrium computation, including policy-gradient methods for imperfect-information games.
question: How can learning dynamics compute equilibria in large imperfect-information games?

name: Improbable AI Lab (Pulkit Agrawal)
primary: RL for robot locomotion and manipulation
topics: legged locomotion;dexterous manipulation;continual learning;whole-body control;sim-to-real rl
summary: Builds machines that learn continuously from interaction, using reinforcement learning for locomotion, dexterous manipulation and continual learning.
question: How can machines automatically and continuously learn about their environment?

name: Learning & Intelligent Systems Group (Leslie Kaelbling; Tomás Lozano-Pérez)
topics: pomdps;task and motion planning;model learning;belief-space planning;robot manipulation
summary: Combines reinforcement learning, model learning and task-and-motion planning to build robots that act under uncertainty in unstructured environments.
question: What principles let robots with imperfect sensors and incomplete knowledge perform everyday tasks?

name: Reliable Autonomous Systems Lab (REALM) (Chuchu Fan)
primary: safe RL and certified learning for control
topics: safe multi-agent rl;control barrier functions;offline rl;reach-avoid;llm planning
summary: Develops certified learning-based control, including safe multi-agent RL with control barrier functions, RL for reach-avoid problems and offline RL.
question: How can learning-enabled autonomous systems be made certifiably safe?

name: Asuman Ozdaglar group (Asuman Ozdaglar)
topics: multi-agent rl;imperfect-information games;graph-structured mdps;alignment;optimization
summary: The group studies optimisation and multi-agent learning, including policy-gradient methods for games and RL on graph-structured MDPs.
question: How do learning agents reach good outcomes when they interact strategically?

name: Ida Momennejad (Microsoft Research NYC)
topics: successor representation;planning;multiscale predictive representations;compositional reasoning;neuroai
summary: Studies how natural and artificial agents build internal models for memory and planning, combining RL, human behavioural experiments and evaluation of reasoning in language models.
question: How do learning, memory, reasoning and agency interact to support flexible planning in natural and artificial intelligence?

name: Microsoft Research NYC Reinforcement Learning Group (Akshay Krishnamurthy; Dylan Foster)
topics: rl theory;contextual bandits;exploration;imitation learning;rl post-training of language models
summary: Develops statistical and computational foundations for RL, bandits and imitation learning, and applies them to pre-training, post-training and exploration in language models.
question: What are the statistical and computational foundations of learning from interaction and feedback over time?

name: NVIDIA GEAR Lab (Jim Fan; Yuke Zhu)
topics: humanoid foundation models;sim-to-real rl;dexterous manipulation;visual rl;gr00t
summary: Builds generalist embodied agents and humanoid foundation models (GR00T) and uses sim-to-real RL for vision-based dexterous humanoid manipulation.
question: How can generalist embodied agents be built that act across virtual worlds and physical humanoid robots?

name: NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab (Yashraj Narang)
topics: sim-to-real transfer;contact-rich assembly;kinesthetic teaching for rl;robot simulation;reward models
summary: Develops simulation-based robot learning methods, including RL with kinesthetic teaching and simulation-in-the-loop sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich manipulation.
question: How can simulation and learning be combined so robots acquire contact-rich manipulation skills that transfer to the real world?

name: EMERGE Lab (Eugene Vinitsky)
topics: multi-agent rl;self-play;driving simulation;human modeling;transportation
summary: The lab builds multi-agent reinforcement learning methods and fast simulators, using large-scale self-play for autonomous driving and transportation.
question: How can large-scale multi-agent learning and simulation produce capable, safe autonomous systems?

name: Hartley Lab (Catherine Hartley)
topics: value-guided choice;predictive representations;structure learning;development
summary: The lab characterises how learning, memory and value-based decision processes develop from childhood to adulthood, using reinforcement-learning models such as predictive representations.
question: How do the learning, memory and decision-making processes that shape behaviour change across development?

name: Mattar Lab (Marcelo Mattar)
primary: planning and replay in the brain
topics: planning;replay;memory sampling;options;human decision making
summary: The lab uses experiments and reinforcement-learning models to study how the brain simulates the future to guide decisions, including planning, replay and memory sampling.
question: How does the brain simulate the future to guide decisions?

name: Zhengyuan Zhou group (Zhengyuan Zhou)
institution: New York University (Stern School of Business)
topics: distributionally robust rl;concurrent rl;bandits;operations;game theory
summary: The group studies data-driven decision making, including distributionally robust and concurrent reinforcement learning and bandits for operations.
question: How can decision policies learned from data remain robust in operational settings?

name: General Robotics & AI Lab (GRAIL) (Lerrel Pinto)
institution: New York University; Meta Superintelligence Labs
topics: robot learning;rl for adaptation;dexterous manipulation;behavior modeling;open-source robots
summary: Works on robot learning, including reinforcement learning for adaptation, action and behavior modeling, and low-cost open-source robots.
question: How can robots learn general skills from data and adapt them in homes and other real environments?

name: Game Innovation Lab (Julian Togelius)
primary: RL and open-ended learning in games
topics: procedural content generation;multi-agent rl;game benchmarks;open-ended learning;quality-diversity
summary: Builds game-based environments and benchmarks for RL and open-ended learning, and trains RL agents for game playing and procedural level design.
question: How can AI systems design their own goals so as to learn surprising skills?

name: Christopher Amato group
topics: cooperative marl;dec-pomdps;multi-robot systems;llm collaboration;rl security
summary: Develops principled methods for multi-agent reinforcement learning and planning under uncertainty with limited communication.
question: How can teams of agents coordinate under uncertainty and limited communication?

name: Generalizable Robotics and AI Lab (GRAIL) (Lawson L.S. Wong)
topics: equivariant rl;on-robot rl;state representations;planning under uncertainty;robot generalization
summary: Studies state representations for robot learning and planning, including approximately equivariant RL architectures and on-robot RL with learned rewards.
question: Which intermediate state representations enable effective robot learning and planning, and therefore robot generalization?

name: Helping Hands Lab (Robert Platt)
topics: equivariant rl;robot manipulation;symmetry;policy learning;grasping
summary: Develops perception, planning and learning methods, including symmetry-aware (equivariant) reinforcement learning, for robot manipulation in unstructured environments.
question: How can symmetry and structure make robot manipulation learning data-efficient?

name: Multimodal and Embodied Reasoning group (Manling Li)
topics: agentic rl;multi-turn rl;world models;vlm agents;multi-agent rl
summary: The group trains language and vision-language agents with multi-turn reinforcement learning and studies world-model reasoning for embodied agents.
question: How can multimodal agents learn to reason and act over many turns through reinforcement learning?

name: Zhaoran Wang group
primary: RL theory and RL for LLMs
topics: rl theory;offline rl;multi-agent rl;llm reasoning;exploration
summary: Works on theoretical foundations of deep reinforcement learning and multi-agent decision making, and on RL methods for language-model reasoning.
question: How can data-driven decision-making methods be made provably efficient?

name: OpenAI RL & Reasoning (Jakub Pachocki)
topics: rl for language models;chain-of-thought reasoning;competitive programming;reward hacking and monitoring;scaling rl
summary: Trains the o-series reasoning models with large-scale reinforcement learning and has published on RL for competitive programming and on monitoring RL-trained reasoning models.
question: How far can scaling general-purpose reinforcement learning take language models on reasoning tasks?

name: Alan Fern group
topics: offline safe rl;learned planning;bipedal locomotion;sim-to-real;explainable rl
summary: Studies RL and planning, including offline safe RL and learned action ranking, and RL for bipedal robot locomotion.
question: How can agents combine learning and planning to make safe, effective sequential decisions?

name: Huazheng Wang group (Huazheng Wang)
topics: bandits;kl-regularized rl;reward poisoning;rl environments;energy systems
summary: The group studies bandits and reinforcement learning under misspecification and adversarial reward corruption, and builds RL environments for energy demand response.
question: How can interactive learning algorithms stay reliable under misspecification and adversarial feedback?

name: Lingzhou Xue group (Lingzhou Xue)
topics: q-learning;federated rl;regret bounds;gap-dependent analysis;statistics
summary: The group studies statistical theory for reinforcement learning, including gap-dependent regret for Q-learning and federated Q-learning.
question: How can model-free reinforcement learning achieve optimal regret with low communication and switching cost?

name: Multi-agent Networks Laboratory (Minghui Zhu)
topics: meta-rl;safe rl;explainable rl;rlhf;multi-agent systems
summary: The lab studies distributed decision making for multi-agent networks, including safe meta-reinforcement learning, explainable RL and RL from human feedback.
question: How can learning agents adapt quickly and safely while explaining their decisions?

name: Physical Intelligence (Karol Hausman; Sergey Levine; Chelsea Finn)
lead: Karol Hausman; Sergey Levine; Chelsea Finn
topics: vision-language-action models;rl from experience;advantage-conditioned policies;real-world robot deployment;robot foundation models
summary: Develops the pi-series robot foundation models and the Recap method for improving vision-language-action policies with RL from autonomous experience and human corrections.
question: How can a general-purpose robot foundation model keep improving from its own real-world experience?

name: Mengdi Wang group (Mengdi Wang)
topics: rl theory;rl for llms;reward models;diffusion models;ai for science
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning theory and RL frameworks for training language and diffusion models, with applications in science and engineering design.
question: How can reinforcement learning make generative models reliable optimisers for scientific and engineering goals?

name: Princeton Reinforcement Learning Lab (Benjamin Eysenbach)
topics: goal-conditioned rl;contrastive rl;unsupervised rl;exploration;scaling rl
summary: Develops reinforcement learning algorithms, with a focus on self-supervised and goal-conditioned methods that propose their own goals and collect their own data.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents learn effectively by proposing their own goals and collecting their own data?

name: Daw Lab (Nathaniel Daw)
primary: model-based vs model-free RL in humans
topics: model-based rl;successor representation;replay;planning;computational psychiatry
summary: The lab uses computational, neural and behavioural methods to study how people and animals learn from rewards and punishments, including model-based planning, replay and successor representations.
question: How do people and animals learn from trial and error to make decisions in computationally demanding sequential tasks?

name: Niv Lab (Yael Niv)
primary: RL and representation learning in the brain
topics: state representation;schemas;medial prefrontal cortex;learning and mental health
summary: The lab builds computational models of how experience changes future choices, focusing on representation learning for RL and its application to mental-health conditions.
question: How does experience change future decisions, and how can computational models of learning inform the treatment of mental-health conditions?

name: Witten Lab (Ilana Witten)
topics: credit assignment;dopamine;value representations;striatum;replay
summary: The lab studies how learning and credit-assignment algorithms map onto brain circuitry, including dopamine value signals and learning from delayed outcomes.
question: How do learning and decision-making algorithms for credit assignment in complex, high-dimensional environments map onto brain circuitry?

name: Chi Jin group
topics: rl theory;multi-agent rl;game theory;llm reasoning;formal theorem proving
summary: Studies the theory and algorithms of reinforcement learning and multi-agent learning, and applies them to LLM reasoning and agents.
question: What makes reinforcement learning and multi-agent learning provably efficient, and how can these ideas improve reasoning agents?

name: Cognitive Robot Autonomy & Learning (CoRAL) Lab (Ahmed H. Qureshi)
topics: motion planning;manipulation;multi-agent planning;policy verification;human-robot collaboration
summary: Researches learning-based planning and control for robots, including reinforcement and imitation learning for manipulation, navigation and multi-agent tasks.
question: How can robots learn to plan and act autonomously in complex, changing environments?

name: Vaneet Aggarwal group
topics: constrained mdps;average-reward rl;policy gradient;robust rl;rl for llms
summary: Studies algorithms and guarantees for reinforcement learning, including constrained, average-reward and robust Markov decision processes.
question: What convergence and regret guarantees are achievable for constrained and average-reward reinforcement learning with general policies?

name: RAI Institute (Marc Raibert)
topics: legged locomotion;sim-to-real rl;wheeled and bicycle robots;athletic control;robot design
summary: Develops RL controllers for dynamic robots such as Spot and the Ultra Mobility Vehicle, including acrobatic bicycle manoeuvres learned with RL.
question: How can learning-based control give robots athletic, dynamic mobility in the real world?

name: He Zhu group (He Zhu)
topics: imitation learning;preference-based rl;temporal logic;program synthesis;safe rl
summary: The group combines programming-languages methods with reinforcement and imitation learning to learn verifiable, specification-compliant policies.
question: How can programmatic structure and formal constraints make learned policies reliable?

name: Rutgers Robot Learning Lab (Abdeslam Boularias)
topics: residual rl;sim-to-real;offline rl;manipulation;vla fine-tuning
summary: Develops reinforcement learning methods for robot manipulation, including residual RL on high of vision-language-action policies and sim-to-real insertion.
question: How can a robot learn from its own experience to perform complex manipulation tasks?

name: Skild AI (Deepak Pathak; Abhinav Gupta)
topics: omni-bodied robot foundation model;physical self-play;sim-to-real rl;locomotion;in-context robot learning
summary: Builds the Skild Brain robot foundation model and post-trains it with reinforcement learning and physical self-play in simulation.
question: Can a single robot brain learn general physical skills across embodiments, improving through reinforcement learning and self-play?

name: Benjamin Van Roy group
topics: posterior sampling;information-directed exploration;bandits;rl from preferences;alignment
summary: Studies data-efficient RL, exploration and bandit theory, including RL from pairwise preferences for long-horizon decisions.
question: How can agents learn efficiently by exploring intelligently and learning from feedback?

name: Emma Brunskill group
topics: offline policy evaluation;offline rl;rl for education;rl for healthcare;confidence intervals
summary: Develops sample-efficient and offline RL methods, including off-policy evaluation with confidence intervals, for education and healthcare applications.
question: How can AI systems learn from few samples to robustly make good decisions in healthcare and education?

name: ILIAD (Dorsa Sadigh)
topics: preference-based reward learning;robot rl;human-robot interaction;q-function scaling;multi-agent interaction
summary: Develops algorithms for agents that interact with humans and other agents, including preference-based reward learning and RL for robot policies.
question: How can AI agents safely and reliably interact with people and other agents?

name: IRIS Lab (Chelsea Finn)
topics: robot rl;expressive policies;batch online rl;meta-learning;rl for llm reasoning
summary: Studies how robots and other agents acquire broadly capable behaviour through learning and interaction, including RL with expressive policies and real-robot RL.
question: How can robots and other agents develop broadly intelligent behaviour through learning and interaction?

name: Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory (Mykel Kochenderfer)
topics: pomdps;safety validation;aerospace autonomy;reward shaping;uncertainty quantification
summary: Develops algorithms for robust sequential decision making under uncertainty, with applications to air traffic control and unmanned aircraft.
question: How can optimal decision strategies be derived efficiently from high-dimensional probabilistic problem representations while maintaining safety?

name: The Movement Lab (C. Karen Liu)
primary: RL for physics-based characters and humanoids
topics: humanoid control;motion tracking;flow policy gradients;physics-based animation;sim-to-real
summary: Develops physics-based control for simulated characters and humanoid robots, including RL motion-tracking controllers, flow-policy gradient methods and real-world policy adaptation.
question: How can simulated characters and humanoid robots learn agile, physically grounded movement and interaction skills?

name: Danijar Hafner (stealth world-model robotics start-up)
institution: Stealth start-up (reported as Embo); formerly Google DeepMind
topics: world models;dreamer agents;imagination training;robot learning;planning
summary: Develops model-based RL agents that learn world models and train inside them (Dreamer series), now applied to robots at a stealth start-up founded after leaving Google DeepMind in late 2025.
question: How can agents learn world models that let them plan and act in situations they have not encountered in training?

name: Jorge Mendez-Mendez group
topics: lifelong learning;compositional rl;robot learning;task and motion planning;modular memory
summary: Studies embodied lifelong learning and compositional structure so that robots and RL agents accumulate and reuse knowledge over time.
question: How can embodied agents accumulate knowledge over their lifetimes to better interact with the world?

name: Dileep Kalathil group
topics: model-based rl;exploration;robust rl;rl for diffusion llms;power systems
summary: Works on reinforcement learning theory and algorithms, including model-based exploration, robustness and RL fine-tuning of language models.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made sample-efficient, robust and safe for real autonomous systems?

name: Tian Lan group (Tian Lan)
institution: The George Washington University (Department of ECE)
topics: multi-agent rl;monte carlo tree search;value function structure;human-ai collaboration
summary: The group develops multi-agent reinforcement learning and multi-agent Monte Carlo tree search methods and studies the structure of value functions.
question: How can many agents plan and learn coordinated policies efficiently in large joint action spaces?

name: Ness Shroff group (Ness Shroff)
topics: safe rl;constrained mdps;multi-objective rl;offline rl;networks
summary: The group develops reinforcement learning with safety constraints and multiple objectives, with theory for linear MDPs and applications in networked systems.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents explore efficiently while respecting safety constraints?

name: Yingbin Liang group
topics: actor-critic;low-rank mdps;rlvr dynamics;sample complexity;optimization theory
summary: Develops provably efficient reinforcement learning algorithms and analyses RL training dynamics, including actor-critic for low-rank MDPs and RL with verifiable rewards.
question: What makes reinforcement learning algorithms provably efficient, and how do their training dynamics behave?

name: Autonomous Systems Group (Ufuk Topcu)
institution: The University of Texas at Austin
topics: safe rl;constrained rl;pomdps;offline rl;formal methods
summary: The group combines formal methods, control and reinforcement learning to build autonomous systems with safety guarantees, including constrained RL curricula and POMDPs under model uncertainty.
question: How can autonomous systems learn while providing verifiable safety guarantees?

name: Agile Robotics and Perception Lab (Giuseppe Loianno)
primary: deep RL for agile aerial robots
topics: quadrotors;learning to fly;fast rl libraries;onboard perception;navigation
summary: Develops perception, learning and control for agile aerial robots, including fast deep-RL tooling (RLtools) for continuous control.
question: How can agile robots navigate complex, dynamic environments using only onboard sensing and learned control?

name: Center for Human-Compatible AI (Stuart Russell)
topics: assistance games;inverse rl;value alignment;offline rl;ai safety
summary: Studies reward learning, assistance games and related decision-theoretic foundations for AI systems that act in humans' interests.
question: How can AI systems be built to be provably beneficial when their objectives are uncertain?

name: Hybrid Robotics Group (Koushil Sreenath)
topics: bipedal locomotion;humanoids;sim-to-real rl;safety filters;quadrupeds
summary: Uses RL and model-based control to produce dynamic, robust locomotion and manipulation on bipedal, humanoid and quadrupedal robots.
question: How can legged robots achieve versatile, dynamic and robust behaviour through learning and control?

name: Hybrid Systems Laboratory (Claire Tomlin)
topics: hamilton-jacobi reachability;safety filters;residual rl;multi-agent coordination;control theory
summary: Combines Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and safety filtering with learning, including residual RL for safe humanoid control.
question: How can learning-enabled autonomous systems be given provable safety guarantees?

name: Robotic AI & Learning Lab (Sergey Levine)
primary: deep RL for robotics and LLMs
topics: offline rl;goal-conditioned rl;robot learning;value-based scaling;rl for language models
summary: Develops deep RL algorithms (offline, goal-conditioned, value-based) and applies them to robot control and language-model agents.
question: How can machines acquire flexible, adaptable behavior autonomously through learning?

name: InterACT Lab (Anca Dragan)
topics: human-ai interaction;reward learning;rlhf;empowerment;alignment
summary: Develops algorithms for agents that learn what people want from interactive human feedback and assist humans, including RL post-training of LLM agents.
question: How can agents learn to do what people actually want through interaction and human feedback?

name: Berkeley Robot Learning Lab (Pieter Abbeel)
topics: model-based rl;value function scaling;humanoid loco-manipulation;flow policies;sim-to-real
summary: Studies scalable deep RL (model-based RL, high-capacity value functions, flow-policy RL) and its use for humanoid and dexterous robot learning.
question: How can robots learn complex skills efficiently through deep reinforcement and imitation learning?

name: Intelligent Dynamics Lab (Roy Fox)
topics: in-sample rl;world models;self-play;observation delays;game theory
summary: Studies structure, exploration and optimization in deep RL, including world-model adaptation, delayed observations and self-play.
question: How do structure, exploration and optimization shape deep control learning in virtual and physical agents?

name: Safe Autonomous Systems Lab (Sylvia Herbert)
topics: hamilton-jacobi reachability;safe rl;dual-objective rl;safety filters;optimal control
summary: Combines Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and optimal control with learning to obtain safety assurances, including RL with reach-avoid objectives.
question: How can autonomous systems obtain scalable safety assurances that adapt quickly to new information?

name: Xiaolong Wang group
institution: UC San Diego; Meta Superintelligence Labs
topics: multitask world models;continuous control;dexterous manipulation;humanoids;reward shaping
summary: Builds world models and RL methods for continuous control and dexterous/humanoid robots.
question: How can embodied agents learn general skills from world models and large-scale data?

name: Lin F. Yang group
topics: sample complexity;constrained mdps;bandits;safe decision making;provable algorithms
summary: Develops fast RL and decision-making algorithms with provable guarantees, including sample complexity of constrained MDPs.
question: How can decision-making algorithms be made fast, safe and provably efficient under uncertainty?

name: UCLA AGI Lab (Quanquan Gu)
topics: contextual bandits;rlhf theory;offline policy learning;thompson sampling;rl for llms
summary: Studies theory and algorithms for bandits, offline policy learning and RL from human feedback for language models.
question: What are the foundations of reinforcement learning and generative AI, and how can they accelerate discovery?

name: Vision and Autonomy Intelligence Lab (Bolei Zhou)
primary: RL for driving and urban agents
topics: driving simulation;metadrive;learning from interventions;navigation;scenario generation
summary: Builds simulators (e.g. MetaDrive, UrbanVerse) and RL/human-in-the-loop learning methods for autonomous driving and urban navigation.
question: How can efficient, generalizable physical AI be built that aligns with humans in complex urban environments?

name: Foster Lab (David Foster)
topics: hippocampal replay;goal-directed navigation;dopamine;offline planning
summary: The lab records hippocampal place-cell sequences in rodents to study how replay of experience relates to goals, reward signalling by dopamine and planning of future paths.

name: ICON Lab (Negar Mehr)
topics: multi-agent rl;credit assignment;multi-agent imitation learning;game-theoretic control;safe interaction

topics: rl theory;preference learning;rlhf;llm reasoning;deep learning theory
summary: The group studies the theory of deep learning, reinforcement learning and preference-based fine-tuning of language models.
question: Why do reinforcement learning and preference optimisation work for training modern models?

name: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Lab – CCN (Anne Collins)

topics: reinforcement learning;working memory;habits;executive function;computational modelling
summary: The lab builds and tests computational models of how reinforcement learning interacts with working memory, habits and executive function in human learning.
question: How do multiple brain processes, such as reinforcement learning and working memory, jointly support learning and decision making?

name: Sicun Gao group (Sicun Gao)
topics: policy gradient;on-policy rl;value estimation;control;automated reasoning
summary: The group studies policy optimisation and value estimation in on-policy reinforcement learning and links RL with control and automated reasoning.
question: What makes policy-gradient reinforcement learning succeed or fail on hard control problems?

name: Yuanyuan Shi group (Yuanyuan Shi)
primary: RL for control and energy systems
topics: learning-based control;on-policy rl;lyapunov functions;energy systems;operator learning
summary: The group combines reinforcement learning and control theory for safe learning-based control, with applications in energy systems.

topics: dopamine;retrospective causal learning;anccr;associative learning;reward timing
summary: The lab studies the biological algorithms behind associative learning and decision making, testing retrospective causal-learning accounts of dopamine against temporal-difference RL.

name: Yue Wang group (Yue Wang)

topics: distributionally robust rl;average-reward mdps;robust markov games;offline rl;sample complexity
summary: The group studies distributionally robust reinforcement learning, including robust average-reward MDPs, robust Markov games and model-free robust algorithms with sample-complexity guarantees.
question: How can reinforcement learning policies remain reliable when the deployment environment differs from the training model?

name: Autonomous Decision and Control Lab (Zachary Sunberg)
primary: POMDPs and decision making under uncertainty
topics: pomdps;online planning;markov games;tree search;aerospace autonomy
summary: Develops algorithms for sequential decision making under uncertainty, including online POMDP planning, robustness analysis of POMDP policies and tree search for Markov games.
question: How can autonomous systems make sequential decisions under uncertainty, with an uncertainty-first approach?

name: Nan Jiang group
topics: off-policy evaluation;offline rl;function approximation;sample complexity;rl theory
summary: Builds the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning in the function-approximation setting, including off-policy evaluation and offline RL.
question: When and how can reinforcement learning with function approximation be statistically efficient?

name: R. Srikant group
topics: policy gradient;average-reward mdps;pomdps;stochastic approximation;convergence analysis
summary: Analyses the convergence and scalability of reinforcement learning algorithms, including policy-gradient methods for average-reward MDPs and POMDPs.

summary: The group analyses KL-regularised reinforcement learning, contextual bandits and RLHF, and develops RL training methods for reasoning in large language models.

name: Furong Huang lab
topics: rl with verifiable rewards;rlhf;vision-language models;embodied agents;trustworthy ai
summary: Studies foundation models as decision-making systems, using RL with verifiable rewards and reward modelling to train and align language, vision-language and embodied agents.
question: How can foundation models reason, act, recover from failure and improve as trustworthy decision-making systems?

name: Kaiqing Zhang group
primary: multi-agent RL and learning in games
topics: multi-agent rl;learning in games;equilibrium computation;multi-agent llm training;control
summary: Studies multi-agent reinforcement learning and learning in games, including equilibrium computation and multi-agent training of language models.
question: How can multiple learning agents reach good outcomes when they interact strategically?

name: Autonomous Learning Lab (Bruno Castro da Silva)
topics: hierarchical rl;plasticity;reward selection;diffusion policies;safe rl
summary: Designs general-purpose RL algorithms, including work on plasticity-stability trade-offs, reward selection under limited feedback and diffusion-policy control.
question: How can RL algorithms be made general-purpose and safe enough to solve real-world tasks with little human intervention?

name: Computational Minds and Agent Well-Being Laboratory (Philip Thomas)
topics: safe rl;off-policy evaluation;high-confidence guarantees;agent well-being;computational theories of mind
summary: Works on reinforcement learning with a focus on policy evaluation and safety guarantees, alongside research on computational theories of mind and agent well-being.
question: How can AI systems be designed to optimize task performance while meeting safety guarantees and respecting agent well-being?

name: Safe, Confident, and Aligned Learning + Robotics Lab (SCALAR) (Scott Niekum)
topics: rlhf;imitation learning;safe rl;reward learning;robotics
summary: Develops learning algorithms that enforce safety constraints, provide performance guarantees and align agent objectives with human objectives, using imitation and reinforcement learning.
question: How can AI systems be aligned with human objectives and deployed safely in the real world?

name: Ambuj Tewari group (Ambuj Tewari)
topics: bandits;average-reward mdps;rlhf theory;mobile health;thompson sampling
summary: The group develops bandit and reinforcement learning algorithms, including average-reward linear MDPs and adaptive interventions in mobile health.

summary: Works on reinforcement learning agents that learn in complex, dynamic environments, including questions of agency, world models and game playing.

summary: The group develops robust and risk-averse reinforcement learning and dynamic programming methods that account for model uncertainty.

topics: q-learning;offline rl;return-conditioned learning;in-context policy optimization;rl theory
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning algorithms with theoretical grounding, including Q-learning variants, offline RL and in-context policy optimisation.
question: How can value-based and offline reinforcement learning be made both provable and practical?

name: Thanh H. Nguyen group (Thanh Nguyen)
topics: offline marl;multi-agent imitation learning;preference learning;security games
summary: The group develops offline cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, multi-agent imitation and preference learning, and game-theoretic security models.
question: How can teams of agents learn coordinated policies from fixed or mixed-quality data?

name: Eric Eaton group (Eric Eaton)
topics: lifelong rl;replicability;policy optimization;model-based rl;fairness in rl
summary: The group studies lifelong and continual learning for reinforcement learning, replicable RL and stable high-update-ratio deep RL.
question: How can agents keep learning across many tasks over a lifetime?

summary: Works on robot learning, including frameworks in which foundation models write reward functions, simulation environments and controllers used to train robots with reinforcement learning.
question: How can robots be made easier to teach and more resource-efficient in the physical world?

name: trustml@Penn (Osbert Bastani)

topics: rl for llm reasoning;policy optimization;safe rl;constrained learning;offline optimization
summary: Works on trustworthy machine learning, including reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning and inference-aware policy optimization.

summary: The group studies the statistical theory of reinforcement learning, including inference for TD learning and sample-optimal actor-critic methods.

summary: The group develops statistical and optimisation theory for reinforcement learning, including minimax regret, reward-free exploration and RLVR dynamics.

summary: The group studies online learning, bandits and reinforcement learning theory, including adversarial MDPs and learning in Markov games.

summary: Combines computational human-robot interaction with quality-diversity search and RL to train agents that coordinate with novel partners and to generate test scenarios.

topics: preference-based rl;reward learning;q-learning;human-robot interaction;multi-agent
summary: Develops RL and reward-learning methods that use human preferences and demonstrations for robot learning and human-robot interaction.
question: How can robots learn efficiently and safely from diverse forms of human feedback?

name: Paria Rashidinejad group (Paria Rashidinejad)

summary: The group studies offline reinforcement learning and RL methods for reasoning in language and diffusion language models.

summary: Develops learning methods, including reward learning and sim-to-real policy learning, for manipulating geometrically and perceptually challenging objects.

name: Rahul Jain group

topics: online rl;stochastic control;preference optimization;multi-objective alignment;learning theory
summary: Studies stochastic control, online RL and preference-based optimization for aligning generative models.

name: Machine Intelligence through Decision-making and Interaction (MIDI) Lab (Amy Zhang)

summary: Develops theory and algorithms for reinforcement learning, with a focus on representations that improve generalization, robustness and sample efficiency.

summary: Develops perception and learning methods, including imitation and reinforcement learning, for general-purpose robot autonomy.

summary: Studies how to create complete intelligent agents through machine learning, especially reinforcement learning, multiagent systems and robotics.

summary: Studies theoretical and empirical aspects of reinforcement learning, including convergence of TD learning and Q-learning and in-context RL.

summary: The group studies RLHF theory, bandits and pure-exploration methods, including sampling strategies for preference-based fine-tuning.

summary: Develops data-driven modelling and control methods (e.g. SINDy) and combines learned dynamics models with control and RL for physical systems.

summary: Develops bandit, active-learning and online-RL algorithms with provable guarantees for adaptive data collection.

summary: Combines model predictive control, world models and inverse RL for robot learning, including off-road navigation and imitation from observation.

summary: Studies RL algorithms that use social information in multi-agent and human-AI interaction, including self-play and RL fine-tuning of LLMs.

summary: Works on RL for foundation models, including reward-model evaluation for RLHF and large-scale asynchronous RL for long-horizon search agents.

summary: Designs reinforcement learning algorithms and applies them to robots, including sim-to-real transfer and RoboCup soccer.

summary: Develops theory and algorithms for reinforcement learning, including offline actor-critic methods for average-reward MDPs and stable offline value-function learning.

summary: The group studies the theory and algorithms of reinforcement learning, including offline RL, exploration and outcome-based RL for language-model reasoning.

summary: The lab develops sequential decision-making methods, including planning and RL in non-stationary environments, for transit and emergency-response systems.

summary: The group works on safe and robust reinforcement learning, including constrained offline RL and robustness benchmarks, and on AI safety.
